body.statement:
Suppose \(1<s\le2\), \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), and define \(\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}\) by def:profile-cutoff-center.  There are numerical constants \(a_{\mathrm p}=2^{-30}\), \(A_{\mathrm p}=64\), and a finite \(C_{\mathrm p}=C_{\mathrm p}(s,M)\) such that, if \(mH\kappa_n^2\ge C_{\mathrm p}\log(e/\kappa_n)\), there is an event \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\), determined by folds one and two, for which
\[
 P(\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}^c)
 \le \frac{64}{H}\exp\{-a_{\mathrm p}mH\kappa_n^2\},
\]
the refinement bracket lies in \([c_P-4H,c_P+4H]\) on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\), and, for every \(u\ge16/n\),
\[
 P\bigl(\{|\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}-c_P|>u\}\cap\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\bigr)
 \le A_{\mathrm p}\exp\{-a_{\mathrm p}m\kappa_n^2u\}.
\]
No equality or compatibility between the left and right derivatives at \(c_P\) is assumed.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\beta=s-1\in(0,1]\) and \(f_\ell=\mu_{D,P}^{\ell}\).  By ass:observable-holder-extensions, each side admits a differentiable extension satisfying
\[
 \lVert f_\ell'\rVert_\infty\le M,
 \qquad |f_\ell'(x)-f_\ell'(z)|\le M|x-z|^\beta. \tag{24}
\]
Consequently Taylor's identity and integration of (24) give, for points on the same side,
\[
 |f_\ell(x)-f_\ell(z)-f_\ell'(z)(x-z)|
 \le\frac{M}{s}|x-z|^s. \tag{25}
\]

We first verify the profile geometry.  In \(L^2[-1,1]\), the Gram determinant of \(1,u,(u-q)_+\) is
\[
 \det G_q=\frac{(1-q^2)^3}{18}>0,
 \qquad |q|\le\frac12, \tag{26}
\]
so the projection in def:profile-cutoff-center is well defined.  Direct integration gives
\[
 \lVert k_q\rVert_2^2
 =\langle S_q-\Pi_{\mathcal B_q}S_q,S_q\rangle
 =\frac{1-q^2}{8}\ge\frac{3}{32}. \tag{27}
\]
The projection coefficients are
\[
 \frac{(q-2)(q-1)}{4(q+1)},\qquad
 -\frac{3(q-1)}{4(q+1)},\qquad
 -\frac{3q}{(q-1)(q+1)}, \tag{28}
\]
respectively, whence \(\lVert k_q\rVert_\infty\le9\) uniformly on \(|q|\le1/2\).

Take a window \([z-r,z+r]\) containing \(c_P=z+qr\) with \(|q|\le1/2\).  Expanding the two side regressions at \(c_P\), equations (25)--(27) and the orthogonality of \(k_q\) to \(1,u,(u-q)_+\) yield
\[
 \begin{split}
 \frac1r\int_{z-r}^{z+r}f(x)k_q\!\left(\frac{x-z}{r}\right)dx
 &=d_P\lVert k_q\rVert_2^2+R(z,r,q),\\
 |R(z,r,q)|&\le18M(3r/2)^s.
 \end{split} \tag{29}
\]
The separate slopes disappear because their difference multiplies \((u-q)_+\), which is in \(\mathcal B_q\); this is the precise reason no derivative matching is needed.  If the whole window lies on one true side, the same calculation with a single Taylor polynomial gives
\[
 \left|\frac1r\int_{z-r}^{z+r}f(x)k_q\!\left(\frac{x-z}{r}\right)dx\right|
 \le18M(3r/2)^s. \tag{30}
\]
Since \(r\le H\), \(M H^s=\kappa_n/2^{12}\), \(s\le2\), and (27) holds, the remainder in (29)--(30) is smaller than \(\kappa_n/64\).  Together with \(d_P\ge\kappa_n\), this separates a jump-containing central window from a smooth window by more than \(3\kappa_n/4\) after division by \(\lVert k_q\rVert_2^2\).  Choose a coarse center for which \(c_P\) is in the central half of the window, and choose \(q\) within \(\kappa_n/2^{16}\) of \((c_P-z)/H\).  Formula (28), split at the two step locations, gives \(|J(z,H,q)-J(z,H,q')|\le256|q-q'|\).  The grid replacement therefore changes the normalized population profile by at most \(\kappa_n/256\).  Hence a fold-one window containing \(c_P\) is retained, while any retained window must meet \([c_P-H,c_P+H]\), on the event that every fold-one profile deviation is at most \(\kappa_n/16\).

For one profile summand, (27)--(28) and uniformity of \(X\) give absolute bound \(96/H\) and second moment at most \(96/H\).  The moment-generating-function inequality used in the proof of lem:rectangular-jump-scan-localization therefore gives
\[
 P\{|\widehat J_1-E_P\widehat J_1|>\kappa_n/16\}
 \le2\exp\{-2^{-28}mH\kappa_n^2\}. \tag{31}
\]
There are at most \(32/H\) coarse centers and \(1+2^{16}/\kappa_n\) profile locations per center.  The hypothesis \(mH\kappa_n^2\ge C_{\mathrm p}\log(e/\kappa_n)\) absorbs this factor and one half of the exponent, so the union bound in (31) is at most
\[
 \frac{32}{H}e^{-2^{-29}mH\kappa_n^2}. \tag{32}
\]
The preceding deterministic separation then places the retained hull inside \([c_P-4H,c_P+4H]\).

Condition on fold one and this coarse event.  Both flank intervals in def:profile-cutoff-center lie wholly on their declared true sides and have Lebesgue length \(H\).  Uniformity of \(X\) makes the population Gram matrix of the rescaled regressors \(1,(X-x_0)/H\) have smallest eigenvalue at least \(H/12\).  Applying (31) to its four entries shows that the empirical smallest eigenvalue is at least \(H/48\), except with probability at most \(8e^{-2^{-28}mH}\).  Equation (25), the normal equations, and the inverse bound \(48/H\) then give
\[
 \max_{x\in B}|\widehat p_\ell(x)-f_\ell(x)|\le\frac{\kappa_n}{64},
 \qquad \ell\in\{-,+\}, \tag{33}
\]
except with probability at most \(16e^{-2^{-28}mH\kappa_n^2}\).  Here the deterministic extrapolation error is at most \(72MH^s<\kappa_n/64\), and the stochastic coefficient error is at most \(\kappa_n/128\) under the stated lower bound on \(mH\kappa_n^2\), after enlarging \(C_{\mathrm p}\).  Clipping cannot increase the error because \(0\le f_\ell\le1\).  Let \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\) be the intersection of the coarse event and (33).  Equations (32)--(33), with \(a_{\mathrm p}=2^{-30}\), prove the first probability display of the lemma.

It remains to analyze fold three.  Conditional on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\), the two predictors are fixed and fold three is independent by ass:iid-sampling.  Put
\[
 q(x)=f_+(x)-f_-(x),\qquad \delta=\kappa_n/64.
\]
For \(0<w\le4H\), equations (24)--(25) give on the right of \(c_P\)
\[
 q(c_P+x)=d_P+ax+r(x),\qquad |a|\le2M,\qquad |r(x)|\le2Mx^s/s. \tag{34}
\]
For every real \(a\), direct minimization gives
\[
 \int_0^w(d_P+ax)^2dx
 =d_P^2w+d_Paw^2+\frac{a^2w^3}{3}
 \ge\frac{d_P^2w}{4}. \tag{35}
\]
Minkowski's inequality, (34), \(w\le4H\), and \(MH^s=\kappa_n/2^{12}\) therefore imply
\[
 \int_0^w q(c_P+x)^2\,dx\ge\frac{1}{8}\kappa_n^2w. \tag{36}
\]
If \(t>c_P\), the conditional population increase in the fold-three criterion is
\[
 \begin{split}
 E_P\{\widehat Q_3(t)-\widehat Q_3(c_P)\mid F_1,F_2\}
 &=\int_{c_P}^{t}\left[(f_+(x)-\widehat p_-(x))^2
 -(f_+(x)-\widehat p_+(x))^2\right]dx\\
 &\ge Q_t-2\delta\sqrt{(t-c_P)Q_t}-\delta^2(t-c_P),
 \end{split} \tag{37}
\]
where \(Q_t=\int_{c_P}^{t}q(x)^2dx\).  Equations (36)--(37) give
\[
 E_P\{\widehat Q_3(t)-\widehat Q_3(c_P)\mid F_1,F_2\}
 \ge2^{-5}\kappa_n^2(t-c_P). \tag{38}
\]
The calculation on the left is identical.  Notice that the conditional variance of one loss difference is bounded by
\[
 16\{q(X)^2+\delta^2\}\mathbf 1\{X\text{ lies between }c_P\text{ and }t\}, \tag{39}
\]
and its absolute value is at most \(4(|q(X)|+2\delta)\).  Thus the variance is controlled by the same integrated quadratic quantity that supplies the drift; no treatment-variance lower bound is being used.

Order the fold-three observations by \(X\).  For \(t>c_P+u\), the difference \(m\{\widehat Q_3(t)-\widehat Q_3(c_P)\}\) is a partial sum of the loss differences in (37).  On the dyadic block \(2^ju\le t-c_P<2^{j+1}u\), apply the elementary exponential supermartingale bound following from (39), with parameter truncated at the reciprocal of the displayed absolute bound.  Equations (36), (38), and (39) give
\[
 P\left\{\inf_{2^ju\le t-c_P<2^{j+1}u}
 \widehat Q_3(t)\le\widehat Q_3(c_P)\mid\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\right\}
 \le8e^{-2^{-28}m\kappa_n^2 2^ju}. \tag{40}
\]
The same argument in decreasing \(X\)-order gives (40) to the left.  Replacing \(c_P\) by the closest grid point changes at most a strip of length \(1/n\); the restriction \(u\ge16/n\) absorbs this strip into the drift in (38).  Summing the two geometric series in (40), and using the bracket containment for \(u>4H\), gives
\[
 P\bigl(\{|\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}-c_P|>u\}\cap\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\bigr)
 \le64e^{-2^{-30}m\kappa_n^2u}.
\]
This is the claimed localization tail.  Equations (26)--(29) show explicitly that the argument profiles out, rather than equates, the two side slopes.
body.justification: The residualized-step identity proves that separate side slopes can be profiled out without changing the model class.
body.gap: It repairs the deterministic slope-kink failure of intercept-jump maximization for \(s>1\).
body.consumer: It is the cutoff-localization input to the higher-smoothness detectable-region question.
